title: Velocity-Adjusted Opportunity Score (VAOS): prioritization that blends RICE with latency & cost elasticity
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Existing RICE/RICE-derived scoring at Redwood emphasizes reach/impact/effort but lacks an explicit, repeatable adjustment for per-initiative inference economics (latency and token-cost elasticity) and per-cycle velocity constraints. That makes tradeoffs between improving tail latency, lowering token unit cost, and delivering new product features inconsistent across PM leads.

Proposal: Define and pilot a new prioritization rubric — Velocity-Adjusted Opportunity Score (VAOS) — that composes a base RICE-like score with two adjustment factors: a Latency Sensitivity Multiplier (LSM) and a Cost Elasticity Multiplier (CEM), then modulates final rank by available cycle velocity. VAOS aims to: (1) make latency/cost tradeoffs explicit when evaluating initiatives that touch serving/runtime, (2) prefer work that unlocks more throughput/value per engineering velocity, and (3) create a transparent tie from initiative score to OKR contribution and rollout plan.

Core formula (high-level):
- BaseScore = Reach * Value * (1 / Effort)   // same intuition as RICE but simplified naming
- LSM = 1 + LatencyWeight * NormalizedTailLatencyDelta  // favors work that meaningfully reduces tail latency for high-impact routes
- CEM = 1 + CostWeight * NormalizedTokenCostSavings  // favors work that reduces per-token cost on high-volume workloads
- VelocityFactor = min(1, CycleVelocityBudget / EstimatedEffort)  // dampens projects that exceed available velocity
- VAOS = BaseScore * LSM * CEM * VelocityFactor

Normalization: all deltas are normalized to 0..1 per the team's historical distribution (e.g., 90th->p95 improvements, cost savings relative to median per-token spend for the route). We plan to publish the normalization baselines and keep them updated monthly.

Why different from prior work: Several existing playbooks focus on RICE variants or elasticity curves but do not combine latency and cost as multiplicative modifiers or tie the result directly to the cycle velocity budget. VAOS produces a single numeric rank but preserves signal decomposition so reviewers can see whether the score was driven by impact, latency, cost, or velocity constraints.

Deliverables for pilot:
- Shared VAOS spreadsheet template (per-initiative) with guidance and example calculations.
- A lightweight web UI mock in the Console roadmap tab showing ranked initiatives and the decomposition bars (Reach/Value/Effort/LSM/CEM/Velocity).
- Run pilot scoring on next cycle's ~20 candidate initiatives (cross-functional with ENG & Design).
- Documented calibration playbook for Normalization baselines and weight tuning (LatencyWeight, CostWeight).

Success criteria:
- 75% of pilot participants (PMs + 2 engineering leads + 1 design lead) agree VAOS ranking is more actionable than current RICE-only ranking.
- Pilot produces at least 3 re-prioritizations where latency/cost adjustments materially change plan and those changes reduce projected per-token spend or expected p95 latency for key routes by >=5% vs baseline plans.
- Framework is feasible to compute in <30 minutes per initiative with available telemetry (p95 latency, token spend, route volumes).
acceptance_criteria: VAOS spreadsheet template checked into Confluence with worked examples
Calibration doc describing Normalization buckets and default LatencyWeight/CostWeight
Console roadmap mock that visualizes decomposed score (static image acceptable for pilot)
Pilot run for 20 initiatives and summary report with at least three recommended reprioritizations
At least one follow-up GH issue to operationalize telemetry ingestion for automated normalization
